Financial Crime Investigators

Hover over a card to reveal the role

Forensic accountant

Forensic accountant

A forensic accountant examines financial information to identify fraud, misconduct, or disputes. They analyze records, trace transactions, gather evidence, and support investigations involving embezzlement, financial statement fraud, insurance claims, and other matters. Forensic accountants commonly work for accounting firms, consulting firms, law firms, corporations, government agencies, and insurance companies.

Fraud examiner

Fraud examiner

A fraud examiner investigates allegations of fraud by reviewing financial records, conducting interviews, analyzing evidence, and helping organizations identify weaknesses in their internal controls. Fraud examiners often work in consulting, corporate compliance, internal audit, and investigative roles.

Internal auditor

Internal auditor

Internal auditors evaluate an organization’s processes and controls to identify risks and ensure policies are followed. Their work often includes detecting red flags, investigating unusual transactions, and helping prevent fraud before it occurs.

FBI agent

FBI agent

An FBI agent investigates potential violations of federal law by collecting evidence, conducting interviews, and building cases for prosecution. Agents assigned to financial crimes may investigate fraud, money laundering, public corruption, securities fraud, and other complex financial schemes.

IRS Criminal Investigation (CI) Special agent

IRS Criminal Investigation (CI) Special agent

IRS special agents investigate potential violations of federal tax and other financial crimes. They analyze tax returns, financial records, and income flows to identify tax evasion, fraud, money laundering, and related misconduct.

Financial crimes investigator or Detective

Financial crimes investigator or Detective

Financial crimes investigators work in state and local enforcement agencies to investigate fraud, embezzlement, identity theft, and other financial crimes within their jurisdiction. They gather evidence, interview witnesses and suspects, analyze financial records, and help build criminal cases.

SEC Division of Enforcement

SEC Division of Enforcement

Investigators within the SEC Division of Enforcement examine potential violations of federal securities laws, including accounting fraud, insider trading, and misleading financial reporting. They analyze financial records, gather evidence, and recommend enforcement actions to protect investors and maintain fair markets.

Office of the Inspector General (OIG)

Office of the Inspector General (OIG)

An Office of Inspector General (OIG) investigator examines fraud, waste, abuse, and misconduct within government agencies and programs. They conduct audits and investigations, interview witnesses, and work to protect public funds.
